entities.summary: Karl Nikolaus Fraas, German botanist and agriculturist, was born at Rattelsdorf, near Bamberg. After receiving his preliminary education at the gymnasium of Bamberg, he in 1830 entered the University of Munich, where he took his doctor's degree in 1834. Having devoted great attention to the study of botany, he went to Athens in 1835 as inspector of the court garden; and in April 1836 he became professor of botany at the National University of Athens. In 1842-1843 he returned to Germany because of The Greek Revolution of September 3, 1843 all the foreign professors were expelled from the National University of Athens.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Fraas's work on botany and agriculture contributed to the development of horticulture in Greece and Germany, influencing agricultural practices for decades. His research also laid the groundwork for future botanical discoveries.
